readerAnswers.event: An Ohio man was sentenced on September 8 to 15 years in prison in a case involving threats, cyberstalking and real and AI-generated sexual images of women and children.
readerAnswers.fake: The event in the picture may never have happened. The person targeted, the harassment and the damage to her life can still be real.
readerAnswers.removal: There are two separate jobs here: holding the perpetrator accountable and getting the image taken down.
readerAnswers.action: If this happens to you or someone you know, the FTC’s guide to image-based abuse explains where to start.

terms.digital forgery: A digital forgery can be a fabricated intimate image that appears to show a real person.

explainBack: A fabricated intimate image can target a real person even though the depicted event never occurred. Criminal punishment of the creator and removal of online copies are separate processes with different decision-makers.
unseenTransfer: If a friend finds a fabricated intimate image on a covered service, use the service’s removal route for the image, document whether it acts within the valid-request period, and treat a police report about the person as a separate step.
